This scenario involved an analysis of all nighttime crashes regardless of dimming periods. The scenario included four mixed-effect negative binomial regression models for nighttime after LED conversion, daytime after LED conversion, nighttime before LED conversion, and daytime before LED conversion. This scenario was only conducted for major roadways in the two cities (i.e., C1 and C2 roadways in Cambridge and HPMS roadways in Somerville) due to data availability. The overall goal of this scenario was to compare the adaptive system at o Cambridge and the regular LED system at Somerville for potential differences in safety performance. The comparison was conducted using a multi-prong approach. The different nighttime crash frequencies in the two cities based on the nighttime after LED conversion model were first 67 compared with the daytime model for the same time period to identify if the two lighting systems correlated with significantly different nighttime crash frequencies between the two cities compared to the daytime difference. This difference was then compared with the difference (i.e., between nighttime and daytime crash frequencies) prior to the LED conversion of the two cities to ensure that the modeled safety effects were not due to potential factors that were not accounted in the after-conversion models. • Nighttime crash analysis by dimming schedule. During this analysis, separate models were developed for each dimming period for different types of roadways. This scenario included the following analyses: Nighttime crashes after 8:00 p.m. on C3 roadways for Cambridge and o non-HPMS roadways for Somerville. For this analysis, the team developed two GLMs of ND crash ratios for the before and after LED conversion periods. The purpose of this analysis was to identify potential changes in ND crash ratios that can be potentially attributed to the use of the adaptive system at Cambridge by comparing the ND crash ratios between the two cities with the different LED systems and between the differences of the two cities prior to LED conversion and after the LED conversion. The GLMs were a flexible alternative to t-tests in comparing the means of two samples and were particularly robust for unpaired and unbalanced samples. Nighttime crashes after 10:00 p.m. on C2 roadways for Cambridge and o HPMS roadways for Somerville. The project team developed four negative binomial regression models comparing the nighttime and daytime crash frequencies for the after LED conversion and before LED conversion periods. Nighttime crashes after midnight on C1 roadways for Cambridge and o HPMS roadways for Somerville. The project team developed four negative binomial models during this analysis to account for nighttime, daytime, before LED conversion, and after LED conversion conditions. The modeling results were combined into a dimming effect and a pseudo dimming effect (for the models prior to LED conversion) for a complete understanding of the potential safety effects of the dimmed lighting levels. • Nighttime crash analysis by roadway type, dimming schedule, and lighting levels.
